misclassified_entities.reason: Internal EVM component. The transaction executor is part of the Ethereum client itself that invokes the VM interpreter. It operates within the same process boundary and is not an external entity.
Outbound-only entity. Trace consumers receive data FROM the system (JSON trace output) but do not send data INTO the system. Not a trust boundary concern for input validation.
Outbound-only entity. In this subgraph, peer nodes receive transaction announcements FROM the local node. They do not send data INTO the system in this context.

Threat model entity. This represents an abstract attacker for threat modeling purposes, not a concrete runtime entity that interacts with the system. Attackers are modeled through the entities they impersonate (e.g., network peers).

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Chain (Consensus Layer)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The Ethereum consensus layer provides withdrawal requests and beacon block roots to the execution layer. It operates under a separate security model with validator attestations and finality. While authenticated through the Engine API, execution layer must still validate withdrawal fields and amounts to prevent bugs from causing ETH creation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P network peers transmitting block headers are anonymous participants in the Ethereum network. They may propagate invalid headers, attempt eclipse attacks, or send malformed data. All received headers must be fully validated including parent hash, state roots, and EIP-4844 blob gas fields.

trusted_external_entities.name: Announcing Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers sending eth/68 transaction announcements with type and size metadata are untrusted network participants. They may provide false metadata (lying about transaction size), attempt DoS via large transaction announcements, or propagate invalid transactions. Metadata should be used for filtering but not trusted for resource allocation.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External applications or users submitting transactions via JSON-RPC interface (eth_sendRawTransactionSync). RPC clients may submit malformed transactions, invalid timeout parameters, or attempt resource exhaustion through many synchronous requests. All parameters must be validated and timeouts must be bounded.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Beacon chain provides valid withdrawal requests. Execution layer validates field types (U64 for indices, Address for recipient, U256 for amount) but trusts cryptographic attestation of withdrawal validity.

Block headers from network peers must be fully validated: parent hash chain, ommers hash (empty), state/tx/receipt roots, withdrawal root, blob gas fields, and beacon root. Invalid headers must be rejected without affecting node state.

Transaction announcements contain type, size, and hash metadata. Size metadata may be false - nodes should use it for filtering decisions but verify actual size upon fetch. Bandwidth throttling should be applied per-peer.

RPC requests contain signed transaction data and optional timeout parameter. Timeout must be validated as positive integer not exceeding node-configured maximum. Invalid timeouts should fall back to default (2 seconds recommended). Transaction data validated per eth_sendRawTransaction semantics.

coverage_analysis.notes: 4 entities were misclassified: 1 internal component (TX executor), 2 outbound-only recipients (trace consumer, peer nodes), 1 threat model entity (attacker). 4 valid external entities identified with boundary edges.
